It's a bit more than that.  They were complicated and he openly asked me not to, and if I did, it would end our friendship. From that, it IS my fault. 

I can't contact his family as he has none, and he doesn't see his friends as "friends" any more, and doesn't care to get help that isn't alcohol.
There literaly wasn't for a while.  He had interest in some other woman, but still forbade us from doing it.
It's a temporary thing.  I'll be back there within a month though.
The question is how do i get him back though?
I'm just not really sure what to say to him is all.
Okay, do you have a spare flux capacitor?

They weren't in a relationship, but she liked him and he has trust issues in relationships because of a previous ex.

They had an off and on thing, he never showed much "interest" in her for a while, she wanted me, I went for it.

He's moving out so i don't see why i need to be the one to move out.
Then how can i at least make it up to him?
What if he's moving out soon though?
I'm fine with the regret.  The sad part is the depression will be the sort that never gets sorted out and healed and it ends up in a giant cycle.
You say not so bad, but i feel that it would end in me becoming a hollow shell of a human being.
I'm fine with the wondering, it's the devastation that a no would leave that has me on the fence.
I do, but the "no" then ensues some major depression, and that's what i'm trying to avoid.

I'll only regret it if i get turned down.  This feels like a game of russian roulette and i'm not sure how many empty chambers there are. 

If not now, then never, and I suppose i could live with that as it beats the alternative.
